name: Task_2
description:
Determine the glass transition temperature (Tg) of sodium silicate by quenching a molten configuration using molecular dynamics simulations. Start from the given pre-equilibrated molten sodium silicate structure. Use the provided Buckingham + Coulomb (BKS-type) potential with long-range electrostatics (PPPM) to define interatomic interactions. Perform the cooling and equilibration under zero external isotropic pressure control using NPT ensemble. Cool the system from 4000 K down to 300 K with a cooling rate of 10 K/ps and a pressure damping factor of 10000, then equilibrate the glass formed at 300 K for an additional 100 ps with a pressure damping factor of 5000. Estimate the glass transition temperature Tg by constructing the density\u2013temperature curve and fitting two linear regimes corresponding to the high-temperature (supercooled liquid) and low-temperature (glassy) regions. Do not look the data beyond 2600 K as then the density becomes noisy. Extract Tg as the intersection point of the two fitted lines and report a finite numerical result in Kelvin (K). Determining a stable Tg is required to pass; an unresolved transition or a missing or null Tg receives zero credit.

Preserve the supplied melt and velocities, use a 1 fs timestep and 100 fs thermostat damping, and end after the hold at step 470,000 without resetting steps or reheating. The evaluator fits Tg from the cooling temperature and density samples at measured temperatures no higher than 2600 K. The retained data must independently support a resolved transition, and the reported Tg must agree with the independent estimate within 100 K.

The reported and independently fitted Tg must each lie within 10% of the benchmark physical reference, in addition to agreeing with each other within 100 K.
